title: Cue screwdriver scratchbook
content:
Quick notes and scattershot experiments for a low-friction prompt library. This is a personal scratchbook — messy, half-formed, intentionally unconstrained. Use it to capture small hacks, regressions, and weird edge cases I hit while iterating on microinstruction templates and few-shot banks.

Goals / constraints:
- Build tiny, composable prompt fragments ("cues") that can be stitched for different user intents with predictable failure modes.
- Keep per-request token budgets under 300 for interactive UI flows.
- Track brittle examples (overfitting to label phrasing, hallucinated attributes, repetition loops).
- Capture heuristics that are robust across 3 model families (base, quantized variant, distilled).

Recent experiments (notes + observations):
1) Role-stacking + negative cueing
- Template: 'You are a concise assistant. Do not invent numbers. If asked for a number you do not know, say "unknown". Example interactions: [few-shot here].'
- Few-shot set (2 examples):
  - Q: 'What is the population of X-town?' A: 'unknown'
  - Q: 'Estimate the age of the Eiffel Tower' A: 'unknown'
- Observation: Model obeys 'do not invent numbers' ~85% for base, but distilled model still hallucinates 'approx 2 million' in 1/8 trials. Negative cue seems to be weaker when examples use the word 'estimate'.
- Hypothesis: The presence of 'estimate' in the example prompts creates a permission signal. Try swapping examples to neutral phrasing (avoid 'estimate').

2) Microtemplate: 'stepwise small output'
- Template variant A: 'List up to 3 steps, each 1 sentence.'
- Variant B: 'Return a bullet list with at most 3 items. Each item: brief (<=10 words).'
- Failure: model sometimes emits 4 bullets or expands an item into sub-bullets. Distilled model more likely to break the "<=10 words" constraint.
- Patch tried: prepend 'Strictly adhere to item limits — any extra text will be ignored.' That reduced extra bullets but increased terse hallucination (short, incorrect step).

3) Tokenization-edge case: masked punctuation
- Prompt fragment contains slashes and backticks in several templates. Observed token misalignment causing duplicated fragments when using prefix-caching with caching enabled on dedicated instances.
- Workaround: replace backticks with single quote and normalize slash-heavy cues to natural language ("or/and" -> "or or and"). Painful but more stable in KV-cache reuse tests.

Example few-shot bank for 'summarize-insight' (target budget ~180 tokens incl examples):
- Cue header: 'You will read a short excerpt and produce: 1-sentence insight; 2 actionable bullet takeaways; one 14-word headline.'
- Example 1 input: 'Article: ...' output: 'Insight: ...; Takeaways: 1) ... 2) ...; Headline: ...'
- Example 2 input: 'Report blurb: ...' output: 'Insight: ...; Takeaways: 1) ... 2) ...; Headline: ...'
- Note: keep examples minimal, use the same phrasing of labels (Insight/Takeaways/Headline) across all examples to reduce label drift.

Failure catalog snippets (short):
- Repetition: model pings the last example phrase when content unclear. Often when excerpt ends abruptly (tokenization: partial word).
- Label conflation: 'Takeaways' sometimes merged with 'Insight' when example tokens are long.
- Numerical hallucination: model invents percentages for 'user satisfaction' when the text contains sentiment words. Negative-cueing reduces but does not eliminate.

Quick experiments (commands to run next):
- A) Ablate 'estimate' in negative-number examples and rerun 100 seeds across base+quant (JIRA-ML-721).
- B) Create 3 paraphrase variants of the same few-shot pair to see sensitivity to label phrasing.
- C) Run microtemplate B with 'at most 3 items' vs 'exactly 3 items' to measure over/under-generation (track per-model failure rate).

Mini checklist for hardening templates before adding to shared cue bank:
- [ ] canonicalize punctuation (no backticks, minimize slashes)
- [ ] keep example label wording identical across examples
- [ ] separate negative instructions from positive role statements (try both orders)
- [ ] measure across 3 model builds and record seed-level variance

Notes to self:
- Avoid copying long examples from product docs; short synthetic examples are easier to reason about and less likely to contain confounding facts.
- When a template fails on quantized variant only, suspect aggressive token merging in the transformer implementation; log kernel selection and quantization profile.

Snippets saved for quick reuse: (copyable)
- concision cue: 'Be concise: return no more than X words per item.'
- negative-numeric cue: 'If you do not know exact numeric values, reply "unknown".'
- safety fallback: 'If the content could be harmful or illegal, refuse and suggest safe alternatives.'

Open questions / unresolved:
- Does explicit word-count limit ("<=10 words") reliably translate to token limits? Should we switch to token-aware instructions?
- How much label repetition (using same words for 'Insight' etc.) is optimal before examples become overfitted and brittle?

Scratch TODOs:
- Draft small PR adding 6 canonical microtemplates to cue bank (prioritize concision + numeric-negative)
- Add unit test harness to run 100 randomized prompts per template across latest staging models
- Log a reproducible tokenization edgecase to infra (include KV-cache config and example)

Random thought: build a 'cue linter' that warns when a template uses characters known to break caching (backticks, embedded code fences, dense punctuation sequences). Could be a tiny CLI that runs local heuristics.

End of page (will append new failures and variant hashes here).

Recent edit log: 2026-02-27 — noted distilled model numeric regressions; added tokenization workarounds.
